definition.text: (1.) Heb. aven, “nothingness;” “vanity” (Isa. 66:3; 41:29; Deut. 32:21; 1 Kings 16:13; Ps. 31:6; Jer. 8:19, etc.). (2.) ‘Elil, “a thing of naught” (Ps. 97:7; Isa. 19:3); a word of contempt, used of the gods of Noph (Ezek. 30:13). (3.) ‘Emah, “terror,” in allusion to the hideous form of idols (Jer. 50:38). (4.) Miphletzeth, “a fright;” “horror” (1 Kings 15:13; 2 Chr. 15:16). (5.) Bosheth, “shame;” “shameful thing” (Jer. 11:13; Hos. 9:10); as characterizing the obscenity of the worship of Baal. (6.) Gillulim, also a word of contempt, “dung;” “refuse” (Ezek. 16:36; 20:8; Deut. 29:17, marg.). (7.) Shikkuts, “filth;” “impurity” (Ezek. 37:23; Nah. 3:6). (8.) Semel, “likeness;” “a carved image” (Deut. 4:16). (9.) Tselem, “a shadow” (Dan. 3:1; 1 Sam. 6:5), as distinguished from the “likeness,” or the exact counterpart. (10.)
